Results.ReviewText: This is our 4th Weber grill. Overall we are happy with this grill. Just a few things I wanted to mention. I wish the burners went right to left vs. front to back. Easier for indirect heat when you cook ribs due to the length of the ribs. I do not like the cooking grates on this model when you clean them. The angle of the grates and the brush is a little quirky. Grill gets nice and hot to sear steaks. Leaves nice marks. The last Weber grill was a stainless steel model and would not get hot enough to sear steaks properly. The cast iron grates work great.  We bought the Weber grill cover and it is a little different the way it uses the Velcro straps to secure. Time will tell how this will hold tight when it gets windy. Grill is the right size for my wife and I. We like the folding side tables. Does not take up a lot of room when side tables are down and covered.

ClientResponses.Response:
Hi Steve! 
We are sorry to hear you are having some trouble with your grill. It sounds like your grill may be in a safety mode known as “bypass." What’s happening is that the regulator thinks there’s a gas leak, so it reduces the pressure. Follow these instructions to reset the bypass safety mode. This is also the way you would want to start your grill each and every time.

1. Open the lid
2. Make sure all knobs are in the off position
3. Turn your LP tank on all the way
4. Wait 60 seconds
5. Turn the first burner to start/high (first position to the left)
6. Hit your igniter
7. Turn on all remaining burners
8. Close the lid to preheat to 500-550°F

If the grill still does not heat up properly after following these steps, please contact our support team. The hose and regulator carries a 2-year warranty and we will be happy to send you a replacement. Thank you.
ClientResponses.Name: Weber Grills

Results.ReviewText: Ok nothing lasts forever and I use the grill about 2-3x per week all year round and it was a great grill. This is my 4th Weber in 20 years as a homeowner and it's a shame that one part or another rusts out rendering the grill useless at some point. The flavor bars, burners, grates, ignitor and rack inside are all replaceable but the base, which gets exposed most to rain as the cover can't keep it dry, has rusted out causing the grill to start collapsing on the left side and the front door support has rusted out on the bottom. Bottom base and columns would be better off stainless, like the front door, as it is always wet and rusts out. We have the same problem on our E-310 at our shore place and it only gets 3 years there due to high humidity. The grill top could go another 5 years as it's still in good shape. Tried another brand once and it was much worse basically rusting out in less than a year.
Results.Title: Great Grill but rusts out on bottom after 5 years
